text:
DECISION MEMO — VENDOR SELECTION (YEAR ONE)
To: CFO | From: Priya, Procurement | Re: Alpha vs. Beta

RECOMMENDATION
Approve Alpha. Beta cannot enter production because SSO is unavailable with no committed delivery date. The cheaper option is non-compliant with a mandatory constraint.

COST COMPARISON (Year One, USD)

| Line item            | Alpha    | Beta     |
|----------------------|----------|----------|
| Annual subscription  | $72,000  | $60,000  |
| One-time setup       | $20,000  | $10,000  |
| Total commit         | $92,000  | $70,000  |
| Budget ceiling       | $100,000 | $100,000 |
| Headroom             | $8,000   | $30,000  |

CONSTRAINT EVALUATION
- SSO before production (mandatory): Alpha — MET. Beta — NOT MET (no committed delivery).
- Other stated requirements: MET by both.
- Budget ceiling ($100K): Both within.

ANALYSIS
Beta's $22,000 nominal saving is not realizable: production cannot start without SSO, and Beta has no date. Alpha delivers the mandatory capability day one, within budget. Headroom comparing totals in isolation is misleading when a constraint gates go-live.

RISK
Selecting Beta blocks production indefinitely or forces a reactive second procurement mid-year with no contractual remedy or delivery protection. Alpha commits 92% of the ceiling, leaving $8,000 contingency against the mandatory requirement.

ACTION
On CFO approval, Priya executes Alpha's $92,000 commit. Revisit Beta in year two if SSO becomes committable on a defined date; Alpha remains the compliant year-one choice.
